episode_title: Episode 136: Shari Short Went From Solo Practice to 35 Clinicians in 4 Years

real_qa.q: How did Shari Short grow Aloha Counseling from a solo practice to 35 clinicians in four years?
real_qa.r: About four years ago, Shari Short went from a solo practice to 40 employees with approximately 35 clinicians. She transitioned by pivoting into supervision and group practice growth because seeing clients one-on-one meant she wasn't generating income when not working. She emphasizes the importance of having a business background or getting support in business areas, hiring people to do what you cannot do, and promoting supervisors from within through internship, associateship, and leadership pathways.
real_qa.requete: Aloha Counseling group practice growth four years

real_qa.q: What is Shari Short's approach to leadership and family systems in group practice supervision?
real_qa.r: Shari Short implements in-person group consultation every two weeks where interns present their own genograms, and she presents hers annually to demonstrate vulnerability. She is heavily influenced by Bowenian family systems theory from her Family Therapy training and her Leadership Institute of Seattle master's program. She addresses countertransference with employees by understanding that people function like their family systems and that staff project authoritative roles onto leadership, requiring managers to learn skills to handle this tension.
real_qa.requete: Bowenian family systems group practice leadership supervision

real_qa.q: What are Shari Short's core business tenets for maintaining group practice culture?
real_qa.r: Shari Short holds two core tenets as a business owner: first, not everybody is the right fit for her culture and community which emphasizes support over competition and building each other up; second, she hires slowly and fires quickly. These two principles help maintain the culture she is trying to build in her practice.
real_qa.requete: hire slowly fire quickly group practice culture

real_qa.q: How does Shari Short balance writing a book while managing a 35-clinician group practice?
real_qa.r: Shari Short structures time meticulously by planning dedicated daily time for her book and setting clear deadlines. She wrote down specific goals yearly including number of employees, revenue targets, and book completion dates. Everything she has done has surpassed the written goals she set for herself. She emphasizes that if you can go to grad school while raising three children and running a consulting business, you can accomplish anything.
real_qa.requete: writing book while managing group practice time management

real_qa.q: What structural supervision and training methods does Aloha Counseling use for new clinicians?
real_qa.r: Aloha Counseling implements in-person group consultation every two weeks where clinicians and interns present genograms. Many clinicians arriving at the practice have not been trained in family systems and come from online degree programs. Shari Short emphasizes the importance of in-person interaction, noting that some clinicians do their coursework entirely online with AI and do not know how to interact with real people, making hands-on training a critical distinction.
real_qa.requete: group consultation genogram supervision clinical training

guest.bio_context: Shari Short is a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist with over 20 years in practice, following a second career transition from executive coaching consulting. She transitioned from a 15-16 year solo private practice to founding and scaling a group practice to 40 employees and 35 clinicians over four years. She recently completed a book on becoming a confident clinician and is influenced by Bowenian family systems theory and leadership training from the Leadership Institute of Seattle.
